lens: Adversarial values: hostile record data reaching the viewer and the materializer; tamper freshness; non-mutation of run/PxC/testimony; materials.py callable persistence and false hit claims.

findings.claim: RECORD.md:64 ("arrays longer than 200 entries carry the first 200 and a note with the full length") does not hold in the JS runtime, and the two runtimes therefore emit different records for the same value — breaking "both runtimes must speak it exactly". adapters.js `materialize` truncates only a TOP-LEVEL array (`Array.isArray(raw) && raw.length > MAX_ARRAY_ENTRIES`, adapters.js:269-272); pyto/src/pyto/materialize.py:150-163 `_truncate_arrays` recurses into dicts and nested lists. Nothing in RECORD.md, viewer/README.md, CHANGES.md or either test suite records this as deliberate (grep for "nested"/"top-level" across all four: no hits).
findings.required_fix: Make the two agree and pin the answer in RECORD.md. Either (a) recurse in adapters.js `materialize` the way `_truncate_arrays` does, so RECORD.md:64 holds as written for both runtimes, and count the original lengths into the note; or (b) qualify RECORD.md:64 to top-level arrays only and drop the recursion from materialize.py:150-163. JS is the reference for semantics, but RECORD.md:64 is currently unqualified, so option (a) is the fix that leaves the spec text true. Add a cross-runtime case with a nested 1000-entry array to viewer/test/validate_cases.mjs (or the record-schema suite) so the divergence cannot come back silently.

findings.claim: A hit IS claimed for a value that failed to load — not in materials.py, which is honest, but one layer up in the artifact a person reads. run_cached.py writes `"outcome": "hit (disk)"` as a string literal for resolutions 2 (line 214) and 3 (line 217), and `ms_saved_total_for_two_hits` (line 231) multiplies a receipt duration by 2 unconditionally. Neither is derived from `store.counters` or from `child_report["counters"]`, both of which are already in hand at that point (counters is read at line 205, the child's at line 216). This is the "dumb receipts and self-verified" failure origin.md:14-17 names: the ledger asserts the outcome instead of recording it.
findings.evidence:
Made every disk load fail the way a truncated or hand-edited <key>.json does (materials.MaterialsStore.load_value raising ValueError — exactly the case materials.py:236-243 handles correctly), then ran run_cached.run_cached() on a temp store:
  in_process_counters: {'requests': 2, 'hits': 0, 'misses': 2, 'writes': 2}
  resolution 1 -> miss+write
  resolution 2 -> hit (disk)          <-- hits == 0
  resolution 3 -> hit (disk) child_counters={"requests":1,"hits":1,"misses":0,"writes":0}
  ms_saved_total_for_two_hits: 0.085  <-- for two hits that did not happen
Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DiscStudio-staging/c7ad5950-a39c-58bb-9747-e1301075cf94/scratchpad/adv/ledger_claim.py. materials.py itself passed every probe: a truncated, empty, non-JSON and NUL-byte <key>.json each counted a miss, recomputed and returned the right value, and kept hits+misses == requests (materials.py:229-243).
findings.required_fix: Derive each resolution's outcome from the counters delta around the call rather than writing the word: snapshot store.counters before and after each resolve_in_process call and emit "hit (disk)" only when hits incremented, "miss+write" only when misses did; for resolution 3 read child_report["counters"]["hits"]. Compute ms_saved from the number of resolutions that actually hit, not from a hardcoded 2. Add a test that patches MaterialsStore.load_value to raise and asserts the ledger says miss — the assertion the current suite has no way to fail.

findings.claim: `_safe` is not injective, so two distinct invocation ids in one Tick can land on one SVG filename: the second write silently overwrites the first, `tick_sheets` returns the same path twice as if it had written two files, and the placeholder panel for the first invocation names a file that now holds the second invocation's SVG. That is the ledger's annotation anchor (research/tick-observability-ledger.md:91-93, pcr | tick | invocation id | part address) resolving to the wrong material — the sheet points a reader at the wrong picture. validate() enforces unique ids, but uniqueness is lost at materialize.py:639 because every non-[alnum-._] character collapses to '-'.
findings.evidence:
Record with one Tick holding invocations 'a/b' (svg A) and 'a-b' (svg B), plus '../../../etc/passwd' (svg A):
  svg files written: ['tick-000-..-..-escaped...-..-..-etc-passwd.svg', 'tick-000-..-..-escaped.a-b.svg', 'tick-000-..-..-escaped.a-b.svg']
  tick-000-..-..-escaped.a-b.svg -> SVG_B  (invocation 'a/b' lost its own document)
No path traversal: '/' is sanitized, nothing was written outside the requested directory, the SVG bytes are verbatim, and the hostile record did not abort the drawing pass. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DiscStudio-staging/c7ad5950-a39c-58bb-9747-e1301075cf94/scratchpad/adv/sheets.py.
findings.required_fix: Make the filename injective at materialize.py:639: when `_safe(id) != id`, append a short digest of the raw id (e.g. `f"{stem}.{_safe(iid)}-{_digest(iid)[:8]}.svg"`), or keep a per-Tick set of emitted names and suffix a counter on collision. Return the deduplicated path list. Add a test with two ids that sanitize alike asserting two files and two distinct contents.

findings.claim: The one loading path that reads from a server, `?src=`, calls `fetch(src)` with the default cache mode, so a record file that was tampered with after being served once can be answered from the browser's HTTP cache without revalidation (heuristic freshness applies when the static server sends no Cache-Control). Every other path is provably fresh — file picker, drag-and-drop and the embedded block all re-parse the bytes handed to them — so this is the single place where the viewer can silently show a stale value.
findings.evidence: Verified fresh, by tamper, in Node (harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DiscStudio-staging/c7ad5950-a39c-58bb-9747-e1301075cf94/scratchpad/adv/js_hostile.mjs): renderRecord shows the tampered value on the second render; coerceToRecord returns the second document; fromPytoRecord(a) === a (a validating pass-through, no memo); mount() re-loading the SAME file name 'run.json' with a changed value shows TAMPERED and not ORIGINAL, with exactly 1 root node left in #output (the previous render is torn down, not stacked); a tamper that invalidates the record clears the view and reports "counters.invocations: expected 4 ..., got 99" rather than leaving the stale one on screen. The only unproven path is `fetch(src)` at tick-viewer.js:445, which no Node test can exercise and whose freshness is the browser's, not the viewer's.
findings.required_fix: `fetch(src, { cache: 'no-store' })` at tick-viewer.js:445, and say so in viewer/README.md:36-45 beside the same-origin note, so the ?src= path carries the same freshness guarantee the picker and drop paths already demonstrate.

findings.claim: RECORD.md:63 says an over-cap value is omitted "with a note carrying the size and the digest". In the JS runtime the digest is only ever the one the caller passes; `fromWumpusRecords` (adapters.js:632) calls `materialize(...)` with no digest even though it holds the value, so an over-cap Wumpus value emits "digest unavailable" where a digest was computable. The Python side always computes one (materialize.py:563-566, `sha256 = <hex>`), so the same over-cap value is digested in one record and undigested in the other.
findings.evidence:
{"pad": "a"*262144} through both:
  python -> note "json value is 262154 bytes, over the 262144 byte cap; sha256 = 7838565876dada27343bbabcafa52c8072209ed3b66682ef3b6a90c21b02fe87"
  js     -> note "value omitted: 262154 bytes over the 262144-byte cap; digest unavailable"
adapters.js:516 and :520 (the DiscStudio adapter) do pass `material` as the digest; adapters.js:632 (Wumpus) passes nothing. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DiscStudio-staging/c7ad5950-a39c-58bb-9747-e1301075cf94/scratchpad/adv/cross.mjs.
findings.required_fix: In `capped` (adapters.js:283-290), when no digest was supplied and the serialized payload is in hand, compute one (a small hex digest over the JSON text) rather than writing "digest unavailable"; or pass a digest from fromWumpusRecords at adapters.js:632. If neither is wanted, amend RECORD.md:63 to say the digest is present only when the producing runtime has one, so the record stops promising a field it does not always carry.
